# Updates {#admin-updates}

A Kailash installation never updates anything in the background — no
package, lock or tool moves without an explicit action. There are
exactly two ways a system moves forward:

1. **Rebuild against a newer lock** at the operator's own cadence —
   pull the lock delta, review what moved, rebuild.
2. **Adopt a newer release** — take the released lock bump as-is.

Upstream source pins are checked on explicit cadences by machine
(more active tool classes are checked more often), but a check
results in a pull request only when the new revision passes its smoke
check — freshness never lands unreviewed. Release naming and the
staged cut ladder are described in [the release model
chapter](../governance/release-model.qmd).
